verdict: Skydo's page is fetched more often than Xflow's and cited a third as often per fetch (0.35 vs 0.91). The PayPal answer has two halves: platforms for freelancers receiving invoices (Wise, Payoneer, Skydo) and gateways for businesses taking cards (Stripe, Razorpay, Cashfree). Xflow's page covers both halves with a 'best for' line per brand and three text-header cost tables, so ChatGPT builds its whole answer from it. Skydo's page has no Razorpay or Cashfree at all, so it can only supply the freelancer half, and it supplies that half through a logo-header table and a carousel.

diagnosis: The PayPal answer has two halves, invoice receivers and card gateways. Xflow's page covers both with a 'best for' line per brand; Skydo's page has no Razorpay, Cashfree or PayU, so half the answer must come from elsewhere.
ChatGPT's per-brand Best for / Pros / Cons blocks are copied from Xflow's H3 blocks, including the sentence about Skydo. Skydo's own description in the answer was written by Xflow.
Text-header tables with rupee figures at three invoice sizes are the most-copied block. Skydo's numbers are in a calculator and a logo-header table, both unreadable.
Skydo's page keeps the SWIFT, Dodo and remittance-app cards from the shared template; they are not PayPal alternatives anyone asks for and they crowd out the gateways that are.
A page that is fetched 281 times and cited 98 is a structure problem, not a retrieval problem. The URL, title and H1 already win the fetch.
23 CTAs and a carousel with a duplicated first card are the same defects diagnosed on the Wise page.
Xflow labels estimates 'about' and its own number 'exact', dates every regulatory claim, and answers 'will I still get my FIRA' under its own heading. Those three habits are cheap to copy.

One text-header comparison table (Platform / Fee model / Best for / Lands on $1,000) and one cost-by-size table ($2,000 / $5,000 / $10,000), dated 'as of <month> 2026'.
